chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: The divorce of a male slave for his female slave is two divorces, and her waiting period is two menstruations if she menstruates; and if she does not menstruate, then her waiting period is a month and a half.

key_terms.طَلَاقُ الْعَبْدِ لِلْأَمَةِ: Divorce of a male slave for his female slave

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period and divorce procedure for a slave girl in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinct legal status of a slave girl (umm walad) in divorce, specifying a two-pronouncement structure and a waiting period (iddah) of two menstruations or three months, which differs from the three menstrual cycles prescribed for free women in the Quran. This ruling reflects the juristic consensus in Shia fiqh that the iddah of a slave is half that of a free woman, emphasizing the hierarchical distinctions in family law. The hadith serves as a primary textual basis for understanding the practical application of divorce procedures within the domestic sphere of early Islamic society.
